clue.text: A garden plot the children litter

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
litter is straw bedding for animals, so a bed

explanation.surface: Youngsters strew rubbish across a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like a verb about mess, but it is the noun for animal bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedbed is a patch of prepared soil where seeds are sown, a kind of garden plot.

clue.text: Increase of time spent in jail

explanation.definitionFit: An extension of length, and slang for a term behind bars.

clue.text: Account for getting out of flat

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of
a plain is flat land

explanation.surface: Justifying leaving one's apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment; it is level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reasons behind it.

clue.text: Trains first mate, note

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK railway
Eve was Adam's mate, the first woman

explanation.surface: Railway services before a ship's officer, noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' suggests a ship's officer; it is Eve, Adam's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, worth two semibreves.

clue.text: The underworld boss railed when expelled by law

parts.note: Dis is the Roman ruler of the underworld
railed means fenced off with rails, barred

explanation.surface: A gangster ranted when thrown out by the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' suggests a crime lord; it is the god Dis. 'railed' looks like ranted, but it means fenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A disbarred lawyer is struck off and expelled from the legal profession.

clue.text: Person set against work with model

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a poser is someone who models, striking poses

explanation.surface: Someone hostile to a job involving a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone set against a plan is one who resists or objects to it.

clue.text: Church in stone of a rich yellow colour

indicators.note: in places the church abbreviation within the rock

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal

explanation.surface: A church built of golden stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment of a deep yellow-brown shade.

clue.text: He'll buy for cash possibly in nicer surroundings

indicators.note: in with surroundings says one piece sits inside another
surroundings marks the word for nicer as the piece enclosing the rest

parts.note: purer means cleaner, nicer

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of cash may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A shopper pays cash, perhaps in a pleasanter setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators share the container job: 'in' and 'surroundings' together say the anagram of cash sits within the word for nicer. 'He'll buy' is a fair definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will buy is a buyer, the one who pays for goods.

clue.text: The Moslem lady offers fruit

definitions.meaning: the wife or female relative of a Muslim ruler

explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's wife or mother, and a pale dried grape used in baking.

clue.text: Rearrange letters right and left-without sleep maybe

indicators.note: without means outside, so the two side letters go round the rest
maybe signals the letters of sleep in some other order

explanation.surface: A sleepless night on both sides, leading to jumbled letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside: the right and left letters stand on either side of the jumbled sleep, an anagram signalled by 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell a word differently is to put its letters into a new form.

clue.text: Check heartless rogue joining the crowd

indicators.note: taking the heart out of the word rogue leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: the press is a dense crowd, as in the press of people

explanation.surface: Restraining a cold-hearted villain who mingles with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or restrain it.

clue.text: Distressed by the French charges

parts.note: distressed means upset, hurt
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: French accusations cause upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like a noun for accusations; it is the verb meaning rushes headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to rush forward violently, the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: The manufacturer's specification meant dear products

indicators.note: products are things made, so the letters of the fodder are made into something new

explanation.surface: A maker's labelling suggested costly goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'products' is the anagram signal: the letters of MEANT DEAR are worked into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the brand title a maker gives its goods to identify them.

clue.text: Fellow greeting Latin swell

parts.note: a fellow is a male, he
ave is the Latin greeting hail

explanation.surface: A man says hello to a Latin dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like a toff; it is a verb meaning rise and fall, as the sea does.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's swell is its rising and falling, a surge or heave.

clue.text: Close in the finish-and yet never in doubt

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words finish-and yet, running across the join

explanation.surface: A race that was tight at the end yet whose result was always certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like part of 'close finish'; it is the definition, close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by is near enough to be convenient, within reach.

clue.text: Certain policemen fix the standard

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police
to stick is to fix in place

explanation.surface: Some officers set the benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, often just the Yard, is the headquarters of London's police.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure against which others are judged.

clue.text: Control a good man completely put back

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
ST, saint, is crosswordese for a good man
all means completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: Restraining a virtuous fellow and returning him entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something back is to fit it again in its place.

clue.text: Almost imprisoned over unpaid debts and double-dealing

indicators.note: almost means one letter short of the full word for imprisoned

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Nearly jailed for unsettled debts and treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacherous and sly, working harm by stealth.

clue.text: Orders put out for projects

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions are issued for schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projects' looks like a noun meaning schemes; it is the verb, sticks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that projects juts out beyond a surface.

clue.text: Operation of small firm backed in newspapers

indicators.note: in puts the reversed company inside the papers

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front

parts.note: CO, short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Work of a minor company featured in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small firm' means the abbreviation of company; 'backed' turns it round and 'in' places it among the letters for newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of steps or actions toward a result.

clue.text: Sickening cob seen to be in a bad way

indicators.text: to be in a bad way
indicators.note: in a bad way means in a poor state, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A male swan is seen to be in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a male swan, or a sturdy horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive or disgusting to the senses.

clue.text: Blue or quite proper?

definitions.meaning: blue is the colour of the Conservatives

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain blue stands for the Conservative wing of politics, and something correct is also described this way.

clue.text: Forbidding one to distort the expression

parts.note: forbidding means stern, grim
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Stern one twisting his face.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a face in pain or disgust.

clue.text: Snarls if crooked agents keep the money

indicators.note: the crooked agents keep the money as a jailer keeps a prisoner, holding it inside them
crooked means bent, so the letters are set awry

parts.note: L stands for pound, the money unit

explanation.surface: Bad agents keep the cash and quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' turns AGENTS into TANGES, which keeps L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarls are knots or snags of hair or string.

clue.text: Duck like one's water feature

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O
as means like
one's read as one is gives I plus S

explanation.surface: A duck resembling a single garden pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert spring with vegetation round it is a natural source of water.

clue.text: Introduce new cut

indicators.note: new tells the solver to make a fresh arrangement of the word Introduce

explanation.surface: Bring in a fresh cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut, as in prices, is a lowering in amount.

clue.text: Outfit the same? That's tough!

parts.note: a rig is a set of clothes
ID is idem, Latin for the same

explanation.surface: Same clothes again? That's hard luck!
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and unbending, hard to change.

clue.text: Cold, thin wash

parts.note: C stands for cold on taps
lean means thin

explanation.surface: A chilly, watery wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something is to rid it of dirt.

clue.text: Getting all straight at the end of the day

explanation.definitionFit: Levelling a surface makes it flat; the close of the day is its last part before night.

clue.text: What a worker might well assume is long-term

definitions.text: What a worker might well assume
definitions.meaning: assume means put on, as a garment worn over clothes
taken over the whole time span, in general

explanation.definitionFit: A protective garment slipped on at work, and a word for taking everything into account.

clue.text: The eccentric seek and find so it's told

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are set out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange person searches and discovers a secret is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a noun for an odd person; it is the anagram signal. In British school slang, to sneak is to tell tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling tales on someone, schoolboy slang for informing.

clue.text: Making a point if not dim

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
unless means if not

explanation.surface: Being pointed unless it is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim place lacks light, as one with no sunshine does.
